Thanks again for taking the call today, Amit — great to learn more about FinLytics' production plans. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Requirement summary (from our call): you need private connectivity for inference traffic, strict IP allowlisting for egress to external services, and a plan that avoids sending customer data to a public internet endpoint. You're evaluating Private VPC (our Private offering) vs Dedicated with PrivateLink.

- Questions we have to proceed:
  1) Do you prefer AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for the initial pilot?
  2) Can you share the CIDR(s) for the VPC(s) we would peer with and any existing NAT/egress IP constraints?
  3) Any PCI/PHI considerations that would push towards on-prem rather than AWS VPC?

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf and a high-level network-diagram.png to show typical architectures.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sean to provide an options matrix (Private VPC vs Dedicated+PrivateLink vs Hosted) with network implications — by EOD tomorrow.
- Amit to share VPC CIDR and whether FinLytics requires traffic to originate from static egress IPs for downstream allowlists.
- Align on an internal security checklist and sign an NDA if you want us to share detailed network runbooks.

If that looks right, can we schedule a 30-min technical sync Wed or Thu next week?

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the diagram. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We favor PrivateLink for security reasons, but our infra team said VPC peering may be faster to stand up for a short pilot. Open to both.
- Our primary VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16. We also have a management VPC at 10.20.0.0/16.
- Downstream allowlists: third-party data vendors require connections from a set of static IPs (we can provide the list). Ideally Redwood can either provide static egress IPs or a documented NAT hop we can accept.
- No PCI/PHI in the pilot; PII is in-scope and needs to be handled per our DPA.

We're available for a technical sync Wed 11/25 or Thu 11/26 (PST) — Priya will join from infra.

— Amit

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up — networking, PrivateLink/VPC peering, IP allowlists

Thanks, Amit — good details. Quick technical breakdown of options and what we'd need from FinLytics to progress: 

Option A — Redwood Hosted API (not private):
- Pros: fastest to get started; no VPC work needed.
- Cons: traffic goes over public endpoints; only suitable if you can allowlist Redwood public egress IPs (not ideal for your stated needs).

Option B — Redwood Dedicated + PrivateLink:
- Pros: keeps you on Redwood-managed infrastructure but exposes endpoints via AWS PrivateLink (interface ENIs in your VPC). Works well when you need private connectivity but want Redwood to manage the runtime.
- Network requirements: accept interface endpoints in a private subnet; allow traffic from those ENIs to your internal subnets. No peering required.
- Egress/static IPs: if your downstream vendors need static IPs, we can route egress through our NATs with advertised static IPs from the Dedicated environment or set up a controlled egress path. We will need the list of allowed destination IPs to validate.

Option C — Redwood Private (VPC peering or Transit/VPN/on-prem):
- Pros: customer-controlled VPC or on-prem deployment; highest isolation.
- Modes:
  1) VPC Peering: we peer Redwood VPC (or a shared services VPC) with your VPC. Requires non-overlapping CIDRs. You must add route entries to send traffic to Redwood. Works well for low-latency connectivity.
  2) Transit/Direct Connect: if you have a transit gateway or Direct Connect, we can peer to a co-located VPC or connect via VPN. Better for complex topologies.
  3) On-prem: air-gapped or private deployments handled as a separate engagement.
- Network requirements for Private:
  - Non-overlapping CIDRs (confirm 10.10.0.0/16 ok).
  - Security group rules: allow inbound from our service subnets and allow outbound as needed.
  - Route table changes: add a route for Redwood subnets through peering attachment.
  - BGP/advertised routes only if using Transit; otherwise static routes for peering.

Other notes:
- IP allowlists: we can provide static egress IPs from Redwood Dedicated or configure an egress NAT on your side via the peering link. Let us know which vendors require static IPs and we will verify.
- TLS and mutual auth: we support mTLS for service-to-service traffic if you want an additional layer.
- SRV/port list: we'll supply a pared-down list of ports and CIDRs for security approval (I attached vpc-peering-checklist.md for the typical fields we need).

Next steps (technical):
1) Amit/Priya: confirm which option you're leaning toward (PrivateLink vs VPC peering) and provide the list of downstream vendor IPs that require allowlisting.
2) If you choose VPC peering: confirm acceptance of 10.10.0.0/16 (we'll need a non-overlap statement).
3) We'll schedule a 30-minute tech deep-dive to walk through the checklist and share a sample CloudFormation template for PrivateLink setup.

Happy to join the Wed/Thu sync — wed/thu times you proposed work for me.

— Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
